description: Advise whether an employee has a viable ordinary unfair-dismissal claim under the Employment Rights Act 1996 (eligibility, fairness, time limit, compensation).

steps.question: Is the individual an employee who has been dismissed by their employer within the meaning of section 95?
facts_needed: The employment status of the claimant as an employee
Whether the employer terminated the contract (with or without notice), a limited-term contract expired without renewal, or the employee resigned in response to the employer's conduct
The effective date of termination as defined under section 97
steps.if_not_met: The individual has no statutory right under section 94 to claim unfair dismissal in the absence of an employment relationship or a dismissal.

steps.question: Does the employee have the requisite period of continuous employment to qualify for unfair dismissal protection?
facts_needed: Length of continuous employment calculated up to the effective date of termination (including any extension under section 97 for statutory notice under section 86)
Whether the employee has at least two years of continuous service
Whether a statutory disapplication or reduction of the qualifying period applies (e.g., suspension under section 64(2), political opinion or affiliation, or reserve force membership)
steps.if_not_met: The employee is excluded under section 108(1) from bringing an ordinary unfair dismissal claim.

steps.question: Was the complaint presented to an employment tribunal within three months of the effective date of termination (or within an allowable extended period)?
facts_needed: The date the complaint was presented to the employment tribunal
Whether pre-proceedings conciliation statutory extensions apply
If presented out of time, whether it was not reasonably practicable to present the complaint within the primary period and whether it was presented within a reasonable time thereafter
steps.if_not_met: The tribunal will lack jurisdiction to hear the complaint under section 111.

steps.question: Did the employer fail to establish a potentially fair reason for the dismissal, or act unreasonably in treating that reason as sufficient to dismiss?
facts_needed: The principal reason shown by the employer for the dismissal (capability, conduct, redundancy, statutory restriction, or some other substantial reason)
Whether the employer acted reasonably or unreasonably in treating that reason as sufficient, having regard to its size and administrative resources
Equity and the substantial merits of the case
steps.if_not_met: The dismissal is fair under section 98, and the claim for unfair dismissal will fail.

steps.question: Has the employee suffered financial loss attributable to the dismissal that is recoverable as a compensatory award?
facts_needed: Expenses and benefits lost as a result of the dismissal attributable to the employer's conduct
Steps taken by the employee to mitigate their loss
Whether the employee's conduct caused or contributed to the dismissal justifying a reduction
The employee's 52 weeks of pay and the applicable statutory maximum cap under section 124
steps.if_not_met: The employee will not be entitled to a compensatory award under section 123, or any compensatory award will be reduced to zero.
